# Issue 68

Hello\! I’ve been in South Africa for a month and I must say that this experience has been immensely enriching, inspiring, and invigorating. I feel liberated with a newfound sense of self-ownership. I’m very happy. Optimistic. Okay, let’s kick things off with some trends that I think we’ll see more of in tech/media this year. 1\) One of the most important topics that we should all aim to understand and combat is media manipulation and disinformation, notably in the form of [deepfakes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Deepfake). The ethical concerns here are beyond overwhelming. This form of media will often be paired with anonymous or fake accounts, so I suspect those will be on the rise as well. Bots are already here, but I’m talking about sophisticated agents controlling individual, influential, and authentic accounts for direct use cases. They’ll cause ruckus in the echo chambers at the poles of radicalized spectrums, where most sane people don’t frequent. 2\) The groundwork for building and deploying interactive media blossoms through new interfaces, and natural language processing experiences a resurgence. I’ll likely write a post about this in the coming weeks because the systems architecture of interactive media is seriously layered, but tend to think of it as any content that’s conversational (uni, bi, or multi) or generally contains chat-based inputs (voice or text). The audience data will be extremely valuable and sentiment analysis 2.0 will emerge. Avatars are conduits for non-live content, which’ll instigate a new playground for affiliate marketing. 3\) Hyperlocal location data and 3D spatial mapping combine in the mobile augmented world. It’ll be denounced as spyware for advertisers, but will be too early for anyone to really do anything about it. Example, toothpaste companies will know when you’re in the dentist’s office. 4\) Brands will start directly financing and producing long-form content (film, tv, podcasts). They’ll continually have to overpay creatives as penance, but it’ll be labeled as patronage. I revisited my [2018 predictions post](https://mailchi.mp/89b017510d07/temeeco-issue-18) and was slightly surprised that I was on the money with most. Way off the mark with PVOD, oh well. Personal “resolutions” for this year are really basic and I’m already failing miserably: stop biting nails, chew food thoroughly, wake up earlier to exercise, read and write more, and return stateside ready to hit the ground running. That last one is in progress. Professional goals are under wraps. It’s fun to be secretive. Here’s to a big 2019 — let’s make it a good one. That’s all for now. See you next week.
